{C.JOB_CAP}s are custom functions or procedures that {C.TIMESCALE_DB} runs on your schedule. The sections below show how to register one, test it, and change or remove it safely.

<Prerequisites context="procedure">
<PrereqCloudOrSelf />
</Prerequisites>

<DoWithAi />

## Create a {C.JOB}

To create a {C.JOB}, create a [{C.PG} function](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/xfunc.html) or [procedure](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/xproc.html) that you want your database to execute, then set it up to run on a schedule.

<NumberedList>
<NumberedItem title="Define a function or procedure">
Wrap it in a `CREATE` statement:

```sql
CREATE FUNCTION <function_name> (job_id INT DEFAULT NULL, config JSONB DEFAULT NULL)
RETURNS VOID
AS $<variable_name>$
DECLARE
    <declaration>;
BEGIN
    <function_body>;
END;
$<variable_name>$ LANGUAGE <language>;
```

For example, to create a function that reindexes a table within your database:

```sql
CREATE FUNCTION reindex_mytable(job_id INT DEFAULT NULL, config JSONB DEFAULT NULL)
RETURNS VOID
AS $$
BEGIN
   REINDEX TABLE mytable;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
```

`job_id` and `config` are required arguments in the function signature. This returns `CREATE FUNCTION` to indicate that the function has successfully been created.
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Call the function to validate">
```sql
select reindex_mytable();
```

The result looks like this:

```sql
 reindex_mytable
-----------------

(1 row)
```
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title={`Register your ${C.JOB} with \`add_job\``}>
Pass the name of your {C.JOB}, the schedule you want it to run on, and the content of your config. For the `config` value, if you don't need any special configuration parameters, set to `NULL`. For example, to run the `reindex_mytable` function every hour:

```sql
SELECT add_job('reindex_mytable', '1h', config => NULL);
```

The call returns a `job_id` and stores it along with `config` in the {C.TIMESCALE_DB} catalog.

The {C.JOB} runs on the schedule you set. You can also run it manually with [`run_job`](/reference/timescaledb/jobs-automation/run_job) passing `job_id`. When the {C.JOB} runs, `job_id` and `config` are passed as arguments.
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Validate the job">
List all currently registered {C.JOB}s with [`timescaledb_information.jobs`](/reference/timescaledb/informational-views/jobs):

```sql
SELECT * FROM timescaledb_information.jobs;
```

The result looks like this:

```sql
 job_id |           application_name           | schedule_interval | max_runtime | max_retries | retry_period |      proc_schema       |             proc_name             |   owner   | scheduled | fixed_schedule |                                         config                                         |          next_start           |         initial_start         | hypertable_schema | hypertable_name |      check_schema      |               check_name
--------+--------------------------------------+-------------------+-------------+-------------+--------------+------------------------+-----------------------------------+-----------+-----------+----------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+-------------------------------+-------------------------------+-------------------+-----------------+------------------------+-----------------------------------------
   1074 | User-Defined Action [1074]           | 01:00:00          | 00:00:00    |          -1 | 00:05:00     | public                 | reindex_mytable                   | tsdbadmin | t         | t              |                                                                                        | 2026-10-12 09:28:40.657211+00 | 2026-10-12 09:28:40.657211+00 |                   |                 |                        |
      3 | Job History Log Retention Policy [3] | 06:00:00          | 01:00:00    |          -1 | 01:00:00     | _timescaledb_functions | policy_job_stat_history_retention | tsdbadmin | t         | t              | {"drop_after": "1 month", "max_failures_per_job": 1000, "max_successes_per_job": 1000} | 2026-10-12 12:00:00+00        | 2000-01-01 00:00:00+00        |                   |                 | _timescaledb_functions | policy_job_stat_history_retention_check
      1 | Telemetry Reporter [1]               | 24:00:00          | 00:01:40    |          -1 | 01:00:00     | _timescaledb_functions | policy_telemetry                  | postgres  | t         | f              |                                                                                        | 2026-10-13 07:02:01.612712+00 |                               |                   |                 |                        |
(3 rows)
```
</NumberedItem>
</NumberedList>

## Test and debug a {C.JOB}

To debug a {C.JOB}, increase the log level and run the {C.JOB} manually with [`run_job`](/reference/timescaledb/jobs-automation/run_job) in the foreground. Because `run_job` is a stored procedure and not a function, run it with [`CALL`](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-call.html) instead of `SELECT`.

<NumberedList>
<NumberedItem title="Set the minimum log level to `DEBUG1`">
```sql
SET client_min_messages TO DEBUG1;
```
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title={`Run the ${C.JOB}`}>
Replace `<JOB_ID>` with the `job_id` that `add_job` returned:

```sql
CALL run_job(<JOB_ID>);
```
</NumberedItem>
</NumberedList>

## Alter and delete a {C.JOB}

Alter an existing {C.JOB} with [`alter_job`](/reference/timescaledb/jobs-automation/alter_job). You can change both the config and the schedule on which the {C.JOB} runs.

<NumberedList>
<NumberedItem title={`Change a ${C.JOB}'s config`}>
To replace the entire JSON config for a {C.JOB}, call `alter_job` with a new `config` object. Replace `<JOB_ID>` with the `job_id` that `add_job` returned:

```sql
SELECT alter_job(<JOB_ID>, config => '{"hypertable":"metrics"}');
```
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title={`Turn off ${C.JOB} scheduling`}>
To turn off automatic scheduling of a {C.JOB}, call `alter_job` and set `scheduled` to `false`. You can still run the {C.JOB} manually with `run_job`. For example:

```sql
SELECT alter_job(<JOB_ID>, scheduled => false);
```
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Re-enable automatic scheduling">
To re-enable automatic scheduling of a {C.JOB}, call `alter_job` and set `scheduled` to `true`. For example:

```sql
SELECT alter_job(<JOB_ID>, scheduled => true);
```
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title={`Delete a ${C.JOB} with \`delete_job\``}>
Replace `<JOB_ID>` with the `job_id` of the {C.JOB} to delete:

```sql
SELECT delete_job(<JOB_ID>);
```
</NumberedItem>
</NumberedList>

<TestPlan>
target: cloud, self-hosted

1. fork the service
2. [cloud] select the service
3. [self-hosted] run SQL: `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS timescaledb;`
4. run SQL: `CREATE TABLE mytable (id int PRIMARY KEY, note text);`
5. run SQL: `CREATE FUNCTION reindex_job_id() RETURNS int AS $$ SELECT job_id FROM timescaledb_information.jobs WHERE proc_name = 'reindex_mytable' $$ LANGUAGE sql;`
6. run SQL: `CREATE FUNCTION reindex_mytable(job_id INT DEFAULT NULL, config JSONB DEFAULT NULL) RETURNS VOID AS $$ BEGIN REINDEX TABLE mytable; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;`
7. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM pg_proc WHERE proname = 'reindex_mytable'`
8. run SQL: `select reindex_mytable();`
9. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM (SELECT reindex_mytable()) r`
10. run SQL: `SELECT add_job('reindex_mytable', '1h', config => NULL);`
11. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM timescaledb_information.jobs WHERE proc_name = 'reindex_mytable' AND proc_schema = 'public' AND schedule_interval = INTERVAL '1 hour' AND config IS NULL AND scheduled`
12. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM timescaledb_information.jobs WHERE proc_name = 'reindex_mytable' AND application_name = 'User-Defined Action [' || job_id || ']' AND max_runtime = INTERVAL '0' AND max_retries = -1 AND retry_period = INTERVAL '5 minutes' AND next_start <= now() + INTERVAL '1 hour'`
13. run SQL: `SELECT * FROM timescaledb_information.jobs;`
14. run SQL: `SET client_min_messages TO DEBUG1;`
15. run SQL: `CALL run_job(reindex_job_id());`
16. run SQL: `SELECT alter_job(reindex_job_id(), config => '{"hypertable":"metrics"}');`
17. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM timescaledb_information.jobs WHERE proc_name = 'reindex_mytable' AND config = '{"hypertable":"metrics"}'::jsonb`
18. run SQL: `SELECT alter_job(reindex_job_id(), schedule_interval => INTERVAL '2 hours');`
19. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM timescaledb_information.jobs WHERE proc_name = 'reindex_mytable' AND schedule_interval = INTERVAL '2 hours'`
20. run SQL: `SELECT alter_job(reindex_job_id(), scheduled => false);`
21. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM timescaledb_information.jobs WHERE proc_name = 'reindex_mytable' AND NOT scheduled`
22. run SQL: `CALL run_job(reindex_job_id());`
23. run SQL: `SELECT alter_job(reindex_job_id(), scheduled => true);`
24. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM timescaledb_information.jobs WHERE proc_name = 'reindex_mytable' AND scheduled`
25. run SQL: `SELECT delete_job(reindex_job_id());`
26. expect no rows: `SELECT 1 FROM timescaledb_information.jobs WHERE proc_name = 'reindex_mytable'`
</TestPlan>
